subject: Renewal timing and start-date options for PixelWave contract
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@pixelwave.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal timing & start-date options

Hi Grace,

Our renewal for PixelWave's Redwood account comes up end-of-November and the procurement team asked me to clarify a couple of operational items before we move to amendment:

1) Start date options — can we choose either 12/1/2026 or 1/1/2027 depending on when we finish purchase order routing?
2) Proration for partial first term — how do you handle billing if we opt for the Jan start to align with our fiscal calendar?
3) Backfill/credit for additional capacity — our engineering team expects a 30% spike in token usage over the first 90 days post-renewal. Is there a standard short-term buffer you can offer?

Can you share a short memo with the options and any impacts to pricing or SLA so I can send to our CFO and procurement?

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Liu
Procurement Manager | PixelWave
procurement@pixelwave.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@pixelwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timing & start-date options

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up-front, then a proposed approach below: 

Short answers: 
- Start date: Yes — you can elect 12/1/2026 or 1/1/2027. Both are routine; the distinction affects proration and the timing of the first invoice.
- Proration: If you pick 1/1/2027 we can prorate the period 1/1–12/31 to match your fiscal year; alternatively we can invoice for a short stub period (12/1–12/31) if you choose 12/1.
- Backfill/credit: We can offer a temporary backfill credit applied as a usage credit for the first 90 days (typically 10–30% depending on uplift). I can propose 3 options below.

Proposed options for PixelWave (so procurement & finance can pick):
A) Calendar-aligned start (1/1/2027): Full annual term starting Jan 1. Redwood issues a prorated invoice for Jan 1–Dec 31 pricing, with a 90-day usage credit of 20% applied as an account-level credit (appears on invoice).
B) Early start (12/1/2026): Term starts Dec 1. No proration; first invoice covers Dec 1–Nov 30 next year. Offer a 60-day backfill credit of 25% to cover immediate spike.
C) Delayed billing + backfill: Execute amendment with start 1/1/2027 but collect a small reservation deposit in December to guarantee capacity; deposit converted to usage credit over first 90 days (30% equivalent).

Next steps I recommend: 1) Confirm preferred start date, 2) pick one of the credit options, 3) I will kick off an internal alignment with Finance and Legal and return a signed amendment template + DocuSign link.

Attaching a short forecast stub/template that John on your side can fill (PW_Demand_Forecast_Q4.pdf) and a summary of the impact matrix (Redwood_renewal_summary.xlsx).

If helpful, we can set a 20-minute call with Marissa from CS to walk the technical impacts.

Best,
Grace
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal timing & start-date options — PixelWave (need proration + credit guidance)

Team — forwarding PixelWave's ask and my proposed options (see below). TL;DR: customer wants to align to Jan 1 but is willing to start Dec 1 if procurement finishes faster. They need a 90-day buffer for expected spike (est. +30% tokens).

Questions for Finance/Rev: which approach preserves revenue recognition clarity and minimizes billing friction? Specifically: 
- If we do the Jan 1 full-year start with a 90-day usage credit, do we need a deposit to reserve capacity from a capacity-scheduling perspective?
- If we choose a stub-period billing (Dec 1–Dec 31) for a Dec start, how do we handle pro-rated invoices in our billing system (any special GL codes needed)?

Proposed leaning from Sales: Offer Option A (1/1/2027 start + 20% 90-day usage credit) and table the deposit path unless PixelWave requests capacity guarantees. Suggested limit: credit not to exceed $45k.

Attachments: PW_Demand_Forecast_Q4.pdf, Redwood_renewal_summary.xlsx

Thanks — need a quick yes/no so I can finalize the amendment language.

—Grace
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal timing & start-date options — PixelWave (need proration + credit guidance)

Appreciate the clear laydown, Grace. My take: go with Option A (1/1/2027 start) with the 90-day usage credit at 20%. Rationale: aligns with customer fiscal, cleaner invoice cadence, lower ops friction. 

Couple of operational notes for Legal/Finance: 
- Cap the total credit at $50k and mark it as a one-time invoiced credit applied over first two invoices so AR reconciles cleanly.
- No deposit required unless PixelWave explicitly asks for guaranteed dedicated capacity; in that case, ask for a 3-month reservation payment.
- Confirm language for auto-renew remains unchanged; any change would require legal sign-off.

Marissa — can you own the 20-minute tech call and validate the 90-day buffer is sufficient? If they are truly +30% sustained longer than 90 days, we'll convert to a usage tier increase and a committed capacity amendment.

Michael — can Finance confirm the GL/path for a credit applied across invoices (cap and code)?

Ben
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Renewal timing & start-date options — PixelWave (finalizing amendment)

Evan — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal review we recommend the following path so procurement and finance can sign off quickly: 

- Agreed start date: 2027-01-01 (Option A)
- Billing/proration: Term will be Jan 1–Dec 31. No December stub invoice.
- Introductory usage credit: 20% credit applied to usage for the first 90 days after go-live, capped at $50,000. Credit will appear as a negative line item on the first two invoices.
- Capacity guarantee: none required today. If usage stays >30% above baseline beyond 90 days we will propose a committed capacity amendment with tiered pricing.

I've attached the short amendment and added a DocuSign link below for PixelWave's countersignature. Please review and confirm which signatory will execute on your side (CFO or VP Ops). If that's all acceptable I'll send the DocuSign for signature and Marissa will schedule the technical readiness call for the week of Jan 4.

DocuSign (amendment): https://app.docusign.com/recipient/ABC123-amendment
Attachment: PW_amendment_docusign.pdf

Best,
Grace
